You are helping compose a revised research idea JSON. Do NOT search the web or read any files — all information you need is provided below. Your job is to produce the complete revised JSON object with all fields filled in.

## Context

The research idea is "LocoMimicGen". Round 3 reviewer feedback identified 4 fixes. Here is exactly what needs to change and all the facts needed to make those changes:

### Fix 1 — Add EgoHumanoid to landscape (required, 1 paragraph)

EgoHumanoid facts (from paper arXiv:2602.10106, Feb 10, 2026, OpenDriveLab):
- Full title: "EgoHumanoid: Unlocking In-the-Wild Loco-Manipulation with Robot-Free Egocentric Demonstration"
- Authors: Modi Shi, Shijia Peng, Jin Chen, Haoran Jiang, Yinghui Li, Di Huang, Ping Luo, Hongyang Li, Li Chen; Institution: OpenDriveLab
- Robot: Unitree G1 humanoid (1.3m, 29 DoF)
- Four tasks: Pillow Placement (carry to bed), Trash Disposal (insert into container), Toy Transfer (grasp-carry-place), Cart Stowing (multi-phase with cart)
- Data: ~100 VR-teleoperated robot episodes + ~300 egocentric human episodes per task (captured with PICO VR headset + ZED X Mini head-mounted camera)
- Method: co-trains VLA policy on human + robot data via (i) view alignment: depth prediction (MoGe) → point cloud reprojection to robot viewpoint → diffusion inpainting for occluded regions; (ii) action alignment: 6-DoF delta EEF for upper body + discrete locomotion commands + binary gripper
- Results: 78% in lab (vs. 59% robot-only baseline), 82% in unseen environments (vs. 31% robot-only baseline)
- Key contrast with LocoMimicGen: EgoHumanoid requires ~400 demos per task (100 robot + 300 human); LocoMimicGen requires ≤20 teleoperated robot demos total. EgoHumanoid augments via human behavioral diversity across real environments; LocoMimicGen augments via combinatorial spatial synthesis in simulation.
- They are complementary: LocoMimicGen's combinatorially diverse simulation demos could serve as the robot-data component in EgoHumanoid-style co-training; EgoHumanoid's human motion priors could inform stance selection in LocoMimicGen's IRM-guided retargeting.

The EgoHumanoid paragraph must be inserted BEFORE the final "No existing system..." closing paragraph in the landscape section.

### Fix 2 — Combinatorial scaling formula (required, 3-4 sentences)

Add to Contribution (3) in the approach section, right after the "100–1,000× demo expansion" claim:

Formula: K=20 source demos, M=3 subtask phases, P=10 object positions × Q=3 table heights × R=5 obstacle layouts.
- Conservative lower bound (reviewer's formula): K×M×P×Q×R = 20×3×10×3×5 = 9,000 unique trajectories = 450× expansion from 20 seed demos
- Full cross-phase combinatorial composition upper bound: K^M × P×Q×R = 20^3 × 150 = 8,000 × 150 ≈ 1.2M
- Practical 100–1,000× range: reflects compatibility filtering (geometrically infeasible segment pairs discarded); 450× is the validated conservative estimate using the K×M×P×Q×R model

Also add the same formula (condensed) to Contribution 3 in the description field.

### Fix 3 — IRM precomputation cost (required)

IRM precomputation specs:
- One-time offline step, amortized across all tasks
- 6D configuration space: SE(2) base pose (x, y, θ) × squat depth × foot spread × weight distribution
- ~50,000 poses sampled
- Cost: ~3–5 H100-hours for GPU-parallel IK sampling in Isaac Lab

Add to Contribution (2) in approach: note that the reachability map is a one-time offline precomputation (~3–5 H100-hours for IK sampling across ~50K balance configuration poses in 6D space), shared across all tasks, and explicitly budgeted in the resource estimate.

Update resource_estimate for BOTH modes:
- Manual mode: add line item for IRM precomputation; update h100_hours range from "~84–105" to "~87–110" (84+3=87 lower, 105+5=110 upper)
- Human-in-loop mode: add line item for IRM precomputation; update h100_hours range from "~95–125" (which was already inconsistent with the breakdown showing 122–152h) to "~125–157" (122+3=125 lower, 152+5=157 upper)
- Update description field compute summary from "(manual: ~84–105h H100; human-in-loop: ~95–152h H100)" to "(manual: ~87–110h H100; human-in-loop: ~125–157h H100)"

### Fix 4 — Contribution 1 crystallization (optional but strongly recommended)

Add as the OPENING SENTENCE of Contribution (1) in both the approach and description fields:
"By expressing the manipulation stance in the object's SE(3) local frame alongside the arm trajectory, frame-transform retargeting to new object configurations automatically yields a feasible new stance without any separate navigation planning."

### Fix 5 — Two-task evaluation justification (from Issue 4, not labeled as Fix but reviewer says "must proactively address")

Expand the evaluation scope paragraph in approach (currently: "The 2-primary + 1-supplementary structure is explicit: the articulated-object task...") to also address the expected reviewer objection about task count (comparing to DexMimicGen 9 tasks, HumanoidGen 6 tasks/120+ scene variants):

Add three arguments: (a) the scaling law curves (demo efficiency as function of synthetic dataset size) are the primary empirical contribution and are fully established on 2 tasks; (b) both primary tasks exercise all three contributions in combination; (c) DexMimicGen's breadth reuses fixed tabletop infrastructure, whereas LocoMimicGen integrates new IRM machinery into a live loco-manipulation stack — integration depth is the comparable ambition. Also note: the 20-day CoRL timeline from conception to submission motivates execution fidelity over task count.

---

## Complete original JSON to revise

Here is the full original JSON. Produce a COMPLETE revised JSON with ALL fields — do not omit any fields. Apply exactly the fixes described above and nothing else.

```json
{
  "title": "LocoMimicGen: Coupled SE(3) Object-Centric Demo Multiplication for Mobile Humanoid Loco-Manipulation",
  "core_problem": "How can a handful of expensive teleoperated whole-body loco-manipulation demonstrations be multiplied by orders of magnitude across diverse spatial configurations — new object positions, table heights, room obstacle layouts — while maintaining physical validity for the mobile bipedal humanoid platform? Isaac Lab's 2.3 GA release contains three directly relevant prior contributions. PR #3150 (merged Sept 9, 2025) adds the G1 loco-manipulation environment integrating a pretrained RL locomotion policy with Pink IK arm control. PR #3259 ('Adds locomanipulation data generation via disjoint navigation', merged Sept 10, 2025) adds pick-navigate-place phase segmentation with occupancy-map path planning between phases and scene randomization of tabletop positions, navigation destinations, and floor obstacles — making it the closest structural predecessor to LocoMimicGen. PR #3992 (merged Dec 1, 2025) extends the Mimic framework with a 'body end-effector' API and navigation controller integration. Despite this infrastructure, three technical gaps prevent room-level combinatorial scaling: PR #3259 handles navigation 'disjointly' — the manipulation stance (where the robot stands to manipulate) is fixed from the source demo and navigation is handled as path-level occupancy-map planning between fixed phases, NOT as coupled SE(3) object-centric encoding of stances jointly with arm trajectories. None of these PRs enforce arm-reachability constraints on base-pose selection during retargeting — the robot manipulates from whatever stance the source demo used, regardless of arm workspace feasibility for new object positions. And none perform combinatorial composition of subtask segments from multiple source demonstrations. These three absences cap achievable diversity at object-position randomization within a single source demo's reach envelope, rather than the combinatorial room-level scaling that MimicGen achieves for tabletop tasks.",
  "opportunity": "Isaac Lab's 2.3 GA release (PRs #3150, #3259, #3992) now provides the exact scaffolding — G1 environment, pick-navigate-place phase segmentation, occupancy-map path planning, Mimic segmentation framework, and navigation controller integration — needed to build a principled extension. The precise technical gap is narrow but high-impact: adding (1) SE(3) object-centric encoding of navigation stances jointly with arm trajectories into the existing Mimic segment representation (replacing the disjoint path-planning approach of PR #3259 with coupled frame-transform retargeting), (2) stance-conditioned reachability-map-guided base-pose optimization enforcing arm feasibility at each manipulation stance during retargeting (adapting IRM methodology from the mobile-manipulator literature to the bipedal humanoid setting, where the reachability map is conditioned on whole-body configuration rather than just SE(2) base pose), and (3) combinatorial subtask segment composition from multiple source demonstrations. OmniRetarget (Amazon, Sept 2025) addresses humanoid loco-manipulation data generation from MoCap sequences via interaction-mesh Laplacian deformation on the G1, but retargets continuous motion sequences and cannot combinatorially compose segments across scene variants. DemoHLM (Oct 2025) demonstrates generalizable single-demonstration adaptation across 10 G1 loco-manipulation household tasks but the single-demo paradigm limits scaling to spatial interpolation within one source demo's envelope. The three-part Isaac Lab Mimic extension proposed here is tractable within existing infrastructure, precisely bounded against Isaac Lab's own 2.3 baseline (including PR #3259 as the most direct predecessor), and is the missing ingredient for room-level combinatorial scaling.",
  "landscape": "MimicGen (CoRL 2023) decomposes arm demonstrations into object-centric subtask segments and applies SE(3) frame transformations — manipulation-only. DexMimicGen (ICRA 2025) extends this to bimanual dexterous humanoids, still tabletop. HumanoidGen (NeurIPS 2025) uses LLM-driven planning for tabletop dexterous tasks with 120+ scene variants — explicitly excludes locomotion.\n\nIsaac Lab 2.3 loco-manipulation infrastructure comprises three PRs that together form the primary baseline. PR #3150 (merged Sept 9, 2025) adds Isaac-PickPlace-Locomanipulation-G1-Abs-v0, integrating a pretrained RL locomotion policy (velocity commands vx, vy, wz) with Pink IK arm control, achieving 92% success on pick-and-place. PR #3259 ('Adds locomanipulation data generation via disjoint navigation', merged Sept 10, 2025, release/2.3.0) is the closest structural predecessor to LocoMimicGen: it adds pick-navigate-place phase segmentation, occupancy-map-based collision-free path planning between phases, and scene randomization of tabletop object positions, navigation destinations, and floor obstacles. The implementation lives under disjoint_navigation/ and works by (a) recording static manipulation teleoperation with the base stationary, (b) applying Mimic augmentation to manipulation segments, and (c) stitching path-planned navigation trajectories between the resulting phases. Critically, PR #3259 does NOT encode navigation stances in the object's SE(3) local frame — navigation is occupancy-map path planning at the trajectory level, while the manipulation stance (where the robot stands to manipulate) is fixed from the source demo, not retargeted to new object positions. There is no arm-reachability constraint on base-pose selection: if a new object position falls outside the arm workspace at the source demo's stance, the generation produces infeasible trajectories rather than finding a feasible stance. There is no combinatorial composition from multiple source demonstrations. PR #3992 (merged Dec 1, 2025) adds a 'body end-effector' API and get_navigation_state() integration into the Mimic framework but relies on the same state-based navigation repetition/skipping, not object-centric stance encoding.\n\nInverse reachability maps (IRM) for robot base placement are a well-established technique. Vahrenkamp et al. 2013 introduced IRM for robot placement by inverting precomputed reachability maps to generate SE(2) distributions of feasible base poses. Burget et al. (ICRA 2015) applied IRM specifically to humanoid stance selection for grasping tasks — but in a static grasping context where balance is assumed, not within a data-generation retargeting loop. MoMa-Pos (arXiv:2403.19940, Oct 2024 revision, ICRA 2025) integrates IRM with object kinematics for mobile manipulator base placement — applied to wheeled platforms where the reachability function maps over SE(2) base pose only. MoMaGen (arXiv:2510.18316, Oct 2025) imposes reachability as a hard constraint for wheeled bimanual mobile base-pose sampling — again, SE(2) for a wheeled platform. The integration challenge for bipedal humanoids is qualitatively different: on wheeled platforms the base pose fully determines arm workspace, but on bipedal systems arm reachability is conditioned on whole-body stance configuration — COM height, foot placement pattern, and balance state collectively shape the arm workspace. A concurrent planning paper (Murooka et al., arXiv:2505.23505, May 2025) uses forward reachability maps for humanoid loco-manipulation task planning via graph search, but targets autonomous task execution planning, not imitation learning data generation; it does not perform data augmentation, Mimic-style segment composition, or retargeting.\n\nOmniRetarget (Amazon, arXiv:2509.26633, Sept 2025) generates loco-manipulation demonstrations on the G1 via interaction-mesh Laplacian deformation of human MoCap sequences (OMOMO, LAFAN1, in-house). It preserves spatial and contact relationships and enables augmentation across embodiments, terrains, and object configurations. Critically, OmniRetarget (a) requires large MoCap databases rather than small teleoperated G1 demonstrations; (b) retargets continuous motion sequences without decomposing into reusable subtask segments; (c) cannot combinatorially compose segments from different source demos; and (d) targets locomotion-heavy tasks rather than precision manipulation requiring tight coupling between base position and arm workspace.\n\nDemoHLM (arXiv:2510.11258, Oct 2025) segments demonstrations into three stages (locomotion, pre-manipulation, manipulation) and adapts the source trajectory to new initial object/robot poses by modifying high-level stage commands on the G1. It demonstrates 10 loco-manipulation household tasks with sim-to-real transfer. DemoHLM's single-demonstration paradigm limits scaling: each task uses one source demo replayed with modified commands, and 'spatial variation' is object position adjustment rather than room-level layout diversity.\n\nMoMaGen (arXiv:2510.18316, Oct 2025) generates bimanual mobile manipulation demonstrations via constrained optimization (hard reachability + soft visibility) on a wheeled bimanual mobile base. The wheeled platform decouples navigation from balance, making MoMaGen's SE(2) base-pose sampling inapplicable to bipedal humanoids.\n\nVisualMimic (arXiv:2509.20322, IROS 2025) unifies egocentric vision with hierarchical whole-body control via human motion tracking — a different paradigm (video-based policy learning) rather than procedural demonstration generation.\n\nNo existing system applies principled multi-segment object-centric demonstration decomposition with COUPLED SE(3) encoding of both navigation stances and arm trajectories — replacing the disjoint occupancy-map navigation of PR #3259 with frame-transform retargeting of manipulation stances to new object configurations — plus stance-conditioned IRM integration for bipedal humanoids and combinatorial multi-source composition, to enable room-level scaling.",
  "approach": "We propose LocoMimicGen, built as a direct extension of Isaac Lab's 2.3 loco-manipulation infrastructure (PRs #3150, #3259, #3992) with three technical contributions. Starting from ≤20 teleoperated G1 whole-body demonstrations per task, each trajectory is decomposed into coupled subtask phases (locomotion-approach, manipulation-A, transit-locomotion, manipulation-B, return) using the Mimic segmentation API.\n\nContribution (1): Coupled SE(3) object-centric representation. During recording, both arm end-effector waypoints AND locomotion stance poses (base position/orientation at each manipulation phase) are encoded jointly in each relevant object's local SE(3) reference frame — extending Isaac Lab Mimic's existing arm-only object-centric segment representation to include the robot base frame. This is the principled replacement for PR #3259's disjoint approach: instead of fixing the manipulation stance from the source demo and path-planning navigation at the trajectory level, LocoMimicGen retargets navigation stances to new object configurations as a natural byproduct of the SE(3) frame transformation, coupling manipulation and navigation retargeting in a single operation.\n\nContribution (2): Stance-conditioned IRM integration for bipedal humanoid retargeting. Retargeting to a new scene configuration requires solving for new manipulation stances satisfying arm reachability at the transformed object positions. We adapt and integrate inverse reachability map (IRM) methodology (Vahrenkamp et al. 2013; Burget et al. ICRA 2015; MoMa-Pos 2024; MoMaGen 2025) into the Mimic retargeting loop for the bipedal G1. The key integration challenge over prior wheeled-platform work is that bipedal arm reachability is conditioned on whole-body stance configuration — COM height, foot contact pattern, and balance state shape the arm workspace — making the IRM higher-dimensional and configuration-dependent compared to the SE(2) base-pose-only IRMs used in MoMa-Pos and MoMaGen. We pre-compute a stance-conditioned upper-body reachability map for the G1 (IK workspace sampled across a distribution of balance configurations) and solve for new stances via constrained optimization. Navigation segments between planned stances use Isaac Lab's pretrained RL locomotion controller (PR #3150) as a navigation oracle. This is framed as an integration contribution: adapting established IRM methodology to the bipedal context within the Mimic retargeting loop, where no prior work has addressed the stance-conditioned reachability problem for data generation.\n\nContribution (3): Combinatorial multi-source segment composition. Validated subtask segments from different source demonstrations are composed combinatorially across scene variants (object positions spanning the full room, table heights, obstacle placements), achieving 100–1000× demo expansion from ≤20 seed demonstrations per task — a qualitatively different scaling regime from single-demo spatial adaptation (DemoHLM) or disjoint-phase augmentation within a single source demo (PR #3259).\n\nIsaac Lab's GPU-parallel simulation (2048+ G1 environments) with the pretrained RL controller validates physical feasibility; failures trigger local replanning of the base-pose optimization.\n\nWe evaluate on 2 primary loco-manipulation tasks (pick-and-place with navigation; two-phase transit task) plus 1 supplementary task (articulated-object manipulation with approach locomotion, e.g., door/drawer). The 2-primary + 1-supplementary structure is explicit: the articulated-object task involves contact-rich IRM optimization that carries higher debug risk within the CoRL timeline, and we position it as supplementary to protect schedule feasibility while retaining all three contributions in the evaluation. Baselines: Isaac Lab Mimic PR #3259 (disjoint navigation, closest structural baseline), Isaac Lab Mimic PR #3992 (position randomization only), OmniRetarget (single-sequence retargeting), and DemoHLM (single-demo command adaptation). A diffusion policy is trained per task on each generated dataset. Sim-to-real transfer on physical G1 hardware is explicitly future work; the contribution is established through simulation scaling analysis and cross-baseline comparison.",

It does NOT encode navigation stances in the object's SE(3) local frame, does NOT enforce arm-reachability constraints on base-pose selection (making generation infeasible when new object positions fall outside source demo stance's arm workspace), and does NOT compose segments from multiple source demonstrations.\n\nContribution (1): LocoMimicGen adds coupled SE(3) object-centric encoding of locomotion stances jointly with arm end-effector waypoints — the principled replacement for PR #3259's disjoint approach, enabling frame-transform retargeting of both navigation stances and manipulation arm motions simultaneously.\n\nContribution (2): Stance-conditioned IRM integration for bipedal humanoid retargeting. Produce a single, complete JSON object. Every field from the original must appear. Apply exactly the five fixes described above. Do not change anything not covered by the fixes. The "change_type" field should be "minor".

Key structural rules:
- In `landscape`: insert the EgoHumanoid paragraph BEFORE the final "No existing system..." paragraph. - In `approach` Contribution (1): prepend the crystallization sentence AS THE VERY FIRST SENTENCE before "During recording..."
- In `approach` Contribution (2): add the IRM precomputation note after "solve for new stances via constrained optimization" and before "Navigation segments..."
- In `approach` Contribution (3): add the formula derivation AFTER the "100–1,000× demo expansion" sentence
- In `approach` evaluation paragraph: expand with the three-argument justification for 2-task scope, keeping the existing articulated-object risk justification
- In `resource_estimate.manual`: add `"irm_precomputation": "One-time offline: G1 stance-conditioned reachability map construction via IK sampling across ~50K balance configuration poses (6D space: SE(2) base × squat depth × foot spread × weight distribution), GPU-parallel in Isaac Lab: ~3–5 H100h; amortized across all tasks"` and update `h100_hours` to reflect 87–110h total
- In `resource_estimate.human_in_loop`: add same `irm_precomputation` line and update `h100_hours` to reflect 125–157h total
- In `description`: update Contribution 1 opening with crystallization sentence, add formula to Contribution 3, add EgoHumanoid complementary paragraph, update IRM cost note, update two-task justification, update compute numbers to (manual: ~87–110h H100; human-in-loop: ~125–157h H100)

Isaac Lab 2.3 loco-manipulation infrastructure comprises three PRs that together form the primary baseline. PR #3150 (merged Sept 9, 2025) adds Isaac-PickPlace-Locomanipulation-G1-Abs-v0, integrating a pretrained RL locomotion policy (velocity commands vx, vy, wz) with Pink IK arm control, achieving 92% success on pick-and-place. PR #3259 ('Adds locomanipulation data generation via disjoint navigation', merged Sept 10, 2025, release/2.3.0) is the closest structural predecessor to LocoMimicGen: it adds pick-navigate-place phase segmentation, occupancy-map-based collision-free path planning between phases, and scene randomization of tabletop object positions, navigation destinations, and floor obstacles. The implementation lives under disjoint_navigation/ and works by (a) recording static manipulation teleoperation with the base stationary, (b) applying Mimic augmentation to manipulation segments, and (c) stitching path-planned navigation trajectories between the resulting phases. Critically, PR #3259 does NOT encode navigation stances in the object's SE(3) local frame — navigation is occupancy-map path planning at the trajectory level, while the manipulation stance (where the robot stands to manipulate) is fixed from the source demo, not retargeted to new object positions. There is no arm-reachability constraint on base-pose selection: if a new object position falls outside the arm workspace at the source demo's stance, the generation produces infeasible trajectories rather than finding a feasible stance. There is no combinatorial composition from multiple source demonstrations. PR #3992 (merged Dec 1, 2025) adds a 'body end-effector' API and get_navigation_state() integration into the Mimic framework but relies on the same state-based navigation repetition/skipping, not object-centric stance encoding.

Inverse reachability maps (IRM) for robot base placement are a well-established technique. Vahrenkamp et al. 2013 introduced IRM for robot placement by inverting precomputed reachability maps to generate SE(2) distributions of feasible base poses. Burget et al. (ICRA 2015) applied IRM specifically to humanoid stance selection for grasping tasks — but in a static grasping context where balance is assumed, not within a data-generation retargeting loop. MoMa-Pos (arXiv:2403.19940, Oct 2024 revision, ICRA 2025) integrates IRM with object kinematics for mobile manipulator base placement — applied to wheeled platforms where the reachability function maps over SE(2) base pose only. MoMaGen (arXiv:2510.18316, Oct 2025) imposes reachability as a hard constraint for wheeled bimanual mobile base-pose sampling — again, SE(2) for a wheeled platform. The integration challenge for bipedal humanoids is qualitatively different: on wheeled platforms the base pose fully determines arm workspace, but on bipedal systems arm reachability is conditioned on whole-body stance configuration — COM height, foot placement pattern, and balance state collectively shape the arm workspace. A concurrent planning paper (Murooka et al., arXiv:2505.23505, May 2025) uses forward reachability maps for humanoid loco-manipulation task planning via graph search, but targets autonomous task execution planning, not imitation learning data generation; it does not perform data augmentation, Mimic-style segment composition, or retargeting.

OmniRetarget (Amazon, arXiv:2509.26633, Sept 2025) generates loco-manipulation demonstrations on the G1 via interaction-mesh Laplacian deformation of human MoCap sequences (OMOMO, LAFAN1, in-house). It preserves spatial and contact relationships and enables augmentation across embodiments, terrains, and object configurations. Critically, OmniRetarget (a) requires large MoCap databases rather than small teleoperated G1 demonstrations; (b) retargets continuous motion sequences without decomposing into reusable subtask segments; (c) cannot combinatorially compose segments from different source demos; and (d) targets locomotion-heavy tasks rather than precision manipulation requiring tight coupling between base position and arm workspace.

DemoHLM (arXiv:2510.11258, Oct 2025) segments demonstrations into three stages (locomotion, pre-manipulation, manipulation) and adapts the source trajectory to new initial object/robot poses by modifying high-level stage commands on the G1. It demonstrates 10 loco-manipulation household tasks with sim-to-real transfer. DemoHLM's single-demonstration paradigm limits scaling: each task uses one source demo replayed with modified commands, and 'spatial variation' is object position adjustment rather than room-level layout diversity.

MoMaGen (arXiv:2510.18316, Oct 2025) generates bimanual mobile manipulation demonstrations via constrained optimization (hard reachability + soft visibility) on a wheeled bimanual mobile base. The wheeled platform decouples navigation from balance, making MoMaGen's SE(2) base-pose sampling inapplicable to bipedal humanoids.

VisualMimic (arXiv:2509.20322, IROS 2025) unifies egocentric vision with hierarchical whole-body control via human motion tracking — a different paradigm (video-based policy learning) rather than procedural demonstration generation.

EgoHumanoid (Modi Shi et al., OpenDriveLab, arXiv:2602.10106, Feb 2026) addresses in-the-wild loco-manipulation on the Unitree G1 (1.3m, 29 DoF) by co-training a VLA policy on ~100 VR-teleoperated robot episodes plus ~300 egocentric human episodes per task (captured with PICO VR headset and ZED X Mini head-mounted camera), spanning four tasks: Pillow Placement, Trash Disposal, Toy Transfer, and Cart Stowing.
